Do not review prior studies here, present data, or provide methodological details that belong in later chapters.
- Literature Review: Organize prior work by the three sub-themes relevant to EDM electrodes and Hastelloy: electrode materials and tool wear; process parameters and MRR; and surface integrity of nickel‑based superalloys. For each sub-theme, summarise what is established and what is not, and end the chapter with an explicit statement of the research gap this thesis addresses (the missing comparison of composite and conventional electrodes on Hastelloy). Do not present the thesis' own methods or results here.
  - Electrode materials and tool wear: Review the literature that reports tool wear behavior for copper, graphite and composite electrodes in EDM, synthesize mechanisms and reported wear rates across studies, and identify inconsistencies and parameter dependencies relevant to Hastelloy. Only use the available sources to consolidate findings and indicate where evidence is missing for Hastelloy specifically. Do not include new experimental data or propose the thesis methodology here.
  - Process parameters and material removal rate: Compare studies that link EDM process parameters (pulse-on time, pulse-off time, current, voltage, polarity, flushing) to material removal rate (MRR) for copper, graphite and composite electrodes, summarise parameter sensitivities reported, and note which parameter ranges and measurement methods are used. Do not discuss tool wear mechanisms or surface integrity here except insofar as they are directly tied to MRR in reviewed studies.
  - Surface integrity of nickel‑based superalloys: Survey the limited literature on surface integrity (recast layer, microcracking, residual stress, roughness) after EDM of nickel‑based superalloys; indicate that only a thin evidence base exists for Hastelloy and similar alloys and identify which surface phenomena remain uncharacterised for composite electrodes. Only 2 sources are available for this theme; flag it as thin and recommend expansion. Do not present experimental measurements from this thesis here.
  - Gap statement: need for direct comparison on Hastelloy: Synthesize the three sub-theme reviews into a concise gap statement that justifies a controlled experimental comparison of composite versus conventional (copper, graphite) electrodes in EDM of Hastelloy, specifying the missing measurements: comparative tool wear rates, MRR under matched conditions, and systematic surface integrity characterisation. Do not repeat literature summaries; produce a focused research gap and research questions that follow directly from the reviews.
- Methodology: Describe and justify the experimental design, materials, instruments and analysis so another researcher could repeat the comparison between composite and conventional electrodes in EDM of Hastelloy. Specify the Hastelloy grade and sample dimensions, electrode materials (copper, graphite, specified composite), EDM machine model or capabilities, process parameter ranges (pulse-on, current, voltage, polarity, flushing), measurement methods for tool wear rate, MRR and surface integrity (microscopy, profilometry, residual stress measurement), and statistical/uncertainty analysis. State repeatability and reproducibility checks. Do not include measurements or analysis results.
  - Materials and specimen preparation: Specify the Hastelloy alloy used, specimen geometry, surface preparation, and the three electrode types (commercial copper, graphite, and the composite composition and fabrication/ procurement details). Describe electrode geometry and initial measurements. Do not report experimental outcomes or microscopy images.
  - EDM machine setup and process parameters: Report the EDM machine capability and settings, the selection rationale for pulse-on time, current, voltage, polarity and flushing conditions, and how parameters will be controlled and logged. Tie each parameter to its role in answering objectives about MRR and wear. Do not present the run-by-run data here.
  - Measurement methods and uncertainty: Describe procedures for measuring tool wear rate (mass or dimensional loss), calculating MRR, and quantifying surface integrity (profilometry, SEM, cross-section metallography, residual stress method). Specify calibration, measurement resolution, and error propagation/ statistical tests to be used. Do not include measured values.
  - Data analysis and reproducibility: Justify the statistical models (ANOVA, regression, or response-surface modelling) that will identify parameter effects on tool wear and MRR, define significance thresholds, and state how missing data and outliers will be handled. Explain how the analysis links to each objective in the scope. Do not present analysis results or interpreted conclusions.
- Results: Report the experimental findings without interpretation: measured tool wear rates for copper, graphite and composite electrodes; measured MRR under the tested parameter sets; processed surface integrity data (roughness, recast layer thickness, micrographs, residual stress results). Present tables and figures with captions and uncertainty. Organise results so each subsection corresponds to an objective: tool wear, MRR, parameter sensitivities, surface integrity.   - Parameter sensitivity and fitted models: Provide the results of fitted statistical models or response surfaces that quantify parameter effects on tool wear and MRR, include model coefficients, goodness-of-fit metrics and diagnostic plots. Do not interpret model implications beyond reporting fit and significance.
  - Surface integrity results: Report measured surface roughness, recast layer thickness, micrographs and residual stress data for Hastelloy after machining with each electrode. Include representative images and quantitative summaries. Do not interpret whether the observed features are beneficial or detrimental here.
- Discussion: Interpret the results in relation to the literature reviewed: explain differences in tool wear and MRR between composite and conventional electrodes, relate parameter sensitivities to prior findings, and assess surface integrity outcomes for Hastelloy. For each subsection explicitly state which thesis objective it answers. Discuss limitations of the experimental design and measurement methods honestly, and draw out practical implications. Do not restate all literature summaries; focus on points directly relevant to interpreting the results.

Do not downplay limitations or propose untested remedies as results.

Do not make prescriptive claims beyond what the data support.
